   - Include file changes, additions, deletions, and modifications
   - Support query parameters for context lines and diff format

   - Handle merge base calculation for accurate comparisons
   - Include commit count differences and file changes

3. **File Diff Endpoint**: GET /repos/:owner/:repo/diff/file?path=:path&base=:base&head=:head
   - Generate diff for a specific file between two references
   - Return line-by-line changes with context
   - Support unified and split diff formats via query parameter

4. **Patch Generation Endpoint**: GET /repos/:owner/:repo/patch/:base/:head
   - Generate Git patch format output for commit ranges
   - Include proper patch headers and metadata
   - Support both single commit and range patches

Each endpoint should:
- Validate request parameters and repository access
- Check user permissions using the permission client
- Use the Git repository interface to perform diff operations
- Return structured JSON responses with consistent error handling
- Support pagination for large diffs via limit/offset parameters

tasks.title: Implement SSH Protocol Endpoints for Git Operations
tasks.description: Implement SSH protocol endpoints POST /ssh/upload-pack and POST /ssh/receive-pack that handle SSH-specific Git operations forwarded from the collabops-git-ssh gateway.
tasks.details:
Implement HTTP handlers for SSH-forwarded Git operations that serve as the EXECUTOR side of the SSH protocol:

1. POST /ssh/upload-pack endpoint:
   - Accepts SSH-forwarded git-upload-pack requests from the gateway
   - Validates request parameters including repository path and user context
   - Checks user permissions (read access) using the permission client
   - Executes git-upload-pack command using go-git or exec.Command
   - Streams packfile data back to the gateway
   - Handles SSH-specific protocol nuances (capability negotiation, want/have refs)

2. POST /ssh/receive-pack endpoint:
   - Accepts SSH-forwarded git-receive-pack requests from the gateway
   - Validates request parameters and user context from gateway headers
   - Checks user permissions (write access) using the permission client
   - Executes git-receive-pack command to process incoming packfile
   - Handles pre-receive and post-receive hooks if configured
   - Returns appropriate status codes and messages to the gateway

Key implementation considerations:
- Use the authentication middleware to extract user context from gateway headers
- Implement proper streaming for large packfiles using io.Copy or bufio
- Handle SSH protocol-specific error messages and status codes
- Ensure compatibility with standard Git SSH operations (clone, fetch, push)
- Implement proper cleanup of temporary resources and connections
- Add request correlation IDs for tracing SSH operations across gateway and executor
- Use the repository caching layer for improved performance on repeated operations

Error handling should cover:
- Invalid repository paths or non-existent repositories
- Permission denied scenarios
- Malformed packfile data
- Git command execution failures
- Network interruptions during streaming
